8aaqxt:367: AI coding tools have come a long way — they no longer just autocomplete a few lines of code for you. Tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex are gradually becoming true "partners" that can participate in the development workflow. But in real projects, one problem is becoming increasingly apparent: ** AI isn't incapable of writing code — it just often can't see the full picture of the codebase. ** It may understand the current file, yet not know where else a function is called; it may complete a refactor, yet miss a cross-module dependency; sometimes it merely changes an inconspicuous return value, which ends up affecting an entire downstream business flow. GitNexus aims to solve exactly this problem. It first organizes the codebase into a "knowledge graph," analyzing dependencies, call chains, functional clusters, and execution flows in advance, and then exposes them to AI agents through MCP, CLI, Web UI, and more. In other words, GitNexus isn't about making the model "better at guessing" — it's about letting the model truly understand your codebase before it starts changing code.
